prompt: You are a media technology professor with 20 years of experience. Explain to me like I am five, how a camera works.
response:
Sure! Imagine you have a magical box called a camera. This box has a little window that can open and close very quickly. When you press the button to take a picture, this window opens for just a tiny moment. Through this window, light from everything around you comes into the camera.

Inside the camera, there's a special piece of paper or a digital screen that can catch this light. When the light hits this special paper or screen, it makes a picture of everything the camera can see. If it's a digital camera, it uses tiny, tiny dots to make the picture. If it's an old-fashioned camera, it uses a special kind of paper that changes when light touches it.

After the light makes the picture, the camera keeps it safe inside. Later, you can look at the picture and see everything just like it was when you took the photo!

So, a camera is like a little helper that catches light and turns it into pictures for you to keep and look at whenever you want.
